text:
marco: Heads-up — a few example apps started getting weird runtime mismatches after the typegen publish an hour ago. failing CI points to runtime API shape differences (Auth/ClientOptions).
devon: saw the alerts. Any quick repro? which example(s)?
marco: examples/vanilla-web and examples/sdk-playground both failed in the browser build step. stack traces show missing default value on ClientOptions in the built bundle.
yasmin: I grabbed the regen diff from release-bot. It shows typegen v0.8.1 published moments ago with the following note: "perf: refactor client defaults; reorder exports" — no semver rationale.
release-bot: published typegen@0.8.1 at 1873007300. changelog entry: "perf: refactor client defaults; reorder exports". CI artifact: https://ci.internal/release/1873007300
oliver: is this a breaking change? default behavior changing should be a minor/major, not a patch. consumers may rely on implicit default config.
yasmin: agreed. semver policy says behavioral changes > patch. Might be that the change was thought to be internal because everything compiles, but runtimes differ after bundling.
marco: another wrinkle: many example apps have typegen listed with a caret in package.json: "@redwood/typegen": "^0.8.0" so npm resolves ^0.8.1 automatically on install. that allowed the patch to land in CI without explicit bumps.
devon: ugh. lockfiles in examples are often not committed or are ignored by our release CI matrix, so examples keep floating ranges.
yasmin: proposal: immediate mitigations — (1) revert typegen@0.8.1 and publish 0.8.2 that restores previous default semantics, (2) treat the behavior change as a minor and release 0.9.0 behind feature flag, (3) in examples, replace caret ranges with exact pinned versions until we have a stable contract.
oliver: +1. also add a postpublish validation job in the typegen release workflow that runs `yarn --frozen-lockfile --cwd examples/* install && yarn --cwd examples/* build` or at least runs builds for the canonical examples. catches bundling/runtime issues.
marco: can we add a prepublish lint step that runs a compatibility smoke test? something like: generate -> run small runtime smoke using node + esbuild bundle to detect missing side-effects.
yasmin: agreed. but immediate action: who will coordinate the revert?
devon: I can draft the revert PR for the generator that restores the default options. will open PR and tag for revert->publish.
marco: thanks. also open an issue to tighten semver/release guidelines for codegen/typegen. this keeps happening where "internal refactor" slips a behavioral change.
release-bot: note: publishing pipeline currently tags npm with "latest" by default. consider using dist-tag logic for experimental changes (publish with "next") to avoid auto-upgrade via caret ranges.
oliver: yes — use `npm publish --tag next` for anything that modifies runtime defaults until we've validated. then a deliberate minor/major once verified.
yasmin: follow-ups I will own: (A) update release playbook with the postpublish example build checklist and dist-tag guidance, (B) add example package.json audit to CI that flags caret ranges for core infra libs, (C) coordinate with devon on the revert and new release. I'll open a PR for the playbook in docs repo.
marco: small note on changelogs: please include a clear "semver: patch|minor|major - rationale" line in every typegen changelog entry. e.g. "Semver: patch|minor|major - rationale" so consumers can automate decisions.
devon: opened revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/typegen/pull/999 (WIP). running tests locally.
ci-bot: rerun: examples/vanilla-web build queued (pinning local to typegen@0.8.0).
marco: until revert lands we'll pin examples to 0.8.0 in their package.json and add a TODO to remove pin once 0.9.0 is validated.
yasmin: I'll add a small GH Action on publish: 
```yaml
- name: Postpublish example builds
  run: |
    for d in examples/*; do 
      (cd $d && yarn install --frozen-lockfile && yarn build) || exit 1
    done
```
this will surface bundling/runtime issues immediately.
oliver: great. also add a test matrix entry that uses esbuild bundler since esbuild seems more sensitive to export ordering.
marco: final ask — update the devex release checklist and add an automated reminder to change dist-tag if publish notes contain "defaults" or "behavior".
yasmin: will do. logging these action items into the release board now. thanks folks :raised_hands:
marco: thanks. I'll update the examples once the revert PR merges and we re-run the matrix.
release-bot: note appended to release issue: "Ensure semver-impact line in changelog; run example builds postpublish; prefer dist-tag next for uncertain changes."
marco: closing thread for now. tracking in issue #452.
